summary: This diff is purely documentation/planning work: it adds a well-structured security-audit cross-reference evaluation (SECURITY_AUDIT_EVALUATION_2026-07-25.yaml) reconciling ChatGPT's and Z.AI's audits against each other and the real source, a companion 7-phase implementation plan (SECURITY_AUDIT_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-07-25.yaml) that intentionally defers actual code/migration changes to future phase dispatches, a MASTER_INDEX.yaml registry entry, and a minimal, backward-compatible widening of auto_phase_continuation.py's PLAN_GLOB into a PLAN_GLOBS list so the new plan file is auto-discovered. No auth code, RLS policy, or SQL migration is actually modified by this diff itself. I independently verified several of the evaluation's file:line citations (failure-event/route.ts, passcode-login/route.ts, sso/[orgSlug]/acs/route.ts, sso/[orgSlug]/login/route.ts) against the real current source and every one matched exactly, which is strong evidence the evaluation is factually grounded rather than fabricated. All three new/changed YAML files parse cleanly, there are no duplicate registry ids in MASTER_INDEX.yaml (97 entries, checked programmatically), and a filesystem check of both PLAN_DIRS found no pre-existing *_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_*.yaml files that the widened glob could unintentionally sweep up. The diff correctly matches this repo's tier2 path pattern (security-named files) and appropriately defers all real fixes -- including the single high-severity finding (SEC-08, unbounded failure-event rate limiting) -- to separately-reviewed future phases rather than shipping them inline.
issues: Phase 0 in the implementation plan is marked status: done by self-report only; auto_phase_continuation.py's real proof-of-done check requires a merged PR for this same tier2 task, which won't be satisfied until a human merges it. The already_dispatched() heuristic (matching a literal 'phase0' token plus a keyword like 'evaluate' in an existing task/PR's own title/branch) may not recognize this task's own branch/title as a match, creating a real risk that a 30-min cron tick re-dispatches phase_0 as duplicate work before this PR is merged. This mirrors the pre-existing WIRING_ENGINE_PHASE_PLAN precedent rather than being a new flaw, but is worth a human's attention at merge time.

The plan's zero_live_user_risk_note (used to justify phase_2 applying FK/CHECK constraints directly via ADD CONSTRAINT instead of a safer NOT VALID -> VALIDATE pattern) is asserted as an owner directive but isn't independently verifiable from this diff -- a human should confirm this before phase_2 is dispatched, since it will apply a real schema migration.
